title: Malta Year 8 Math — All 19 Chapters: Basic Set E
question: Set E: one quick step from each of the nineteen chapters, with new numbers.
intro: **Set E:** the same 38 steps as Basic, new questions, two per chapter.

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Rocket countdown
questions.prompt:
A rocket clock counts seconds.

It shows \(-8\), which means 8 seconds before lift-off (lift-off is 0).

Then 11 seconds pass.

What does the clock show now?
questions.figure_alt: A number line from −10 to 5. Start at −8; eleven hops of 1 to the right end at a question mark.
questions.solution:
Time passing moves **right** on the number line:

\[-8 + 11 = \boxed{3}\]

\(19\) adds 8 and 11 and forgets that \(-8\) is before lift-off.

questions.title: Ch 1 Directed Numbers · Quiz points
questions.prompt:
In a quiz game your score is \(-3\) points (3 points below zero).

A wrong answer loses 6 points.

What is your score now?
questions.figure_alt: A number line from −10 to 2. Start at −3; six hops of 1 to the left end at a question mark.
questions.solution:
Losing points moves **left** on the number line:

\[-3 - 6 = \boxed{-9}\]

\(3\) adds 6 to \(-3\) instead of taking it away.

questions.title: Ch 2 Number Work · Gozo ferry deck
questions.prompt:
The Gozo ferry carries 2 vans and 4 rows of cars, with 5 cars in each row.

The total is \(2 + 4\times5\).

How many vehicles are there?
questions.figure_alt: A ferry deck from above: two vans and four rows of five cars, then equals a question mark.
questions.solution:
BIDMAS: multiply first (the rows), then add.

\[4\times5 = 20\]

\[2 + 20 = \boxed{22}\]

\(30\) adds first, as if it were \((2 + 4)\times5\).

questions.title: Ch 2 Number Work · Sticker sheet
questions.prompt:
A square sheet of star stickers has 9 rows with 9 stickers in each row.

The number of stickers is \(9^2\) (the small 2 means 9 times itself).

How many stickers are there?
questions.figure_alt: A 9 by 9 square of stickers; how many stickers in all is the question.
questions.solution:
A square number is rows times columns:

\[9^2 = 9\times9\]

\[9\times9 = \boxed{81}\]

\(18\) is \(9\times2\), not \(9\times9\).

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Car park barrier
questions.prompt:
A car park barrier arm lifts up from a straight road.

On one side, the arm makes \(55^\circ\) with the road.

Find the angle between the arm and the road on the other side.
questions.figure_alt: A red and white barrier arm raised from a post on a straight road. On the left the angle with the road is 55°; on the right the angle is a question mark.
questions.solution:
The road is a straight line, so the two angles add up to \(180^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 55^\circ = \boxed{125^\circ}\]

\(305^\circ\) uses \(360^\circ\), which is for angles around a point.

questions.title: Ch 3 Angles · Buoy triangle
questions.prompt:
At the Blue Lagoon, a swim route goes round 3 buoys and makes a triangle.

Two of its angles are \(45^\circ\) and \(100^\circ\).

Find the third angle.
questions.figure_alt: A triangle of three buoys in the sea. One angle is 45°, one is 100° and the top angle is a question mark.
questions.solution:
The angles in a triangle add up to \(180^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 45^\circ - 100^\circ = \boxed{35^\circ}\]

\(215^\circ\) takes the angles from \(360^\circ\); a triangle uses \(180^\circ\).

questions.title: Ch 4 Fractions · Festa nougat
questions.prompt:
A bar of qubbajt (festa nougat) is cut into 7 equal pieces.

A fraction like \(\frac{1}{7}\) means 1 piece out of the 7.

You eat 2 pieces and a friend eats 4 pieces.

What fraction of the bar is eaten?
questions.figure_alt: A nougat bar in 7 pieces: 2 orange pieces (you), 4 green pieces (a friend); the eaten fraction is a question mark.
questions.solution:
Same size pieces, so add the tops:

\[\frac{2}{7} + \frac{4}{7} = \boxed{\frac{6}{7}}\]

\(\frac{6}{14}\) adds the bottoms too, but there are still 7 pieces, not 14.

questions.title: Ch 4 Fractions · Beach trip
questions.prompt:
A class has 25 students.

\(\frac{4}{5}\) of them go on the beach trip (\(\frac{4}{5}\) means 4 out of every 5 equal parts).

How many students go?
questions.figure_alt: 25 students in 5 equal boxes of 5; 4 boxes are shaded and labelled with a question mark.
questions.solution:
Split 25 into 5 equal boxes, then take 4 of them:

\[25\div5 = 5\]

\[5\times4 = \boxed{20}\]

\(5\) is only one box; you need 4 of the 5 boxes.

questions.title: Ch 5 Decimals · Beach umbrella and sunbed
questions.prompt:
At Golden Bay an umbrella costs €6.50 to hire and a sunbed costs €4.20.

How much do they cost together?
questions.figure_alt: A umbrella with a price tag of €6.50 and a sunbed with a price tag of €4.20; beside them the column sum 6.50 + 4.20 with a question mark for the total.
questions.solution:
Line up the decimal points:

\[6.50 + 4.20 = \boxed{10.70}\]

- The answer is €10.70.
- \(0.70\) forgets to carry the 1 ten when \(6 + 4 = 10\) euros.

questions.title: Ch 5 Decimals · Ten steps
questions.prompt:
Each of your steps is 0.75 m long.

You walk 10 steps, which is \(0.75\times10\) metres.

How far do you walk?
questions.figure_alt: Ten items of 0.75 m per step in a row; below, a place-value table with 0.75 in the top row and arrows moving each digit one place left into a row of question marks.
questions.solution:
Every digit moves one place to the left:

\[0.75\times10 = \boxed{7.5}\]

\(75\) moves the digits two places, which is multiplying by 100, not 10.

questions.title: Ch 6 Percentages · Film adverts
questions.prompt:
A film on TV lasts 80 minutes.

\(10\%\) of that time is adverts (\(10\%\) means 10 out of every 100, the same as one tenth).

How many minutes of adverts are there?
questions.figure_alt: A bar for 80 minutes cut into 10 equal blocks; the first block (10%) is a question mark.
questions.solution:
\(10\%\) is one block out of 10:

\[80\div10 = \boxed{8}\]

- So \(10\%\) of 80 minutes is 8 minutes.
- \(70\) takes 10 away; a percentage is a part, not a subtraction.

questions.title: Ch 6 Percentages · Beach umbrellas
questions.prompt:
At Golden Bay there are 100 beach umbrellas in 10 rows of 10.

Some umbrellas are open.

Per cent means out of 100.

What percentage of the umbrellas is open?
questions.figure_alt: A 10 by 10 grid of 100 umbrellas: 7 full rows and 2 more are coloured.
questions.solution:
- Per cent means out of 100.
- Count: 7 full rows and 2 more.

\[70 + 2 = 72\]

\[\frac{72}{100} = \boxed{72\%}\]

\(28\%\) counts the closed umbrellas.

questions.title: Ch 7 Ratio · Beach shells
questions.prompt:
You collect 27 shells at Golden Bay.

White shells and pink shells are in the ratio \(4 : 5\).

How many pink shells are there?
questions.figure_alt: A bar model: four white boxes for white shells, five pink boxes for pink shells, 27 shells in all; the pink share is a question mark.
questions.solution:
There are \(4 + 5 = 9\) equal parts:

\[27\div9 = 3\]

\[3\times5 = \boxed{15}\]

12 is the smaller share; 13.5 splits 27 into 2 halves, but the ratio has 9 parts, not 2.

questions.title: Ch 7 Ratio · Coins in a jar
questions.prompt:
A money jar holds 8 one-euro coins and 32 ten-cent coins.

Write the ratio one-euro : ten-cent, \(8 : 32\), in its simplest form.
questions.figure_alt: Eight silver counters (one-euro coins) in 1 group of 8 and thirty-two gold counters (ten-cent coins) in 4 groups of 8.
questions.solution:
The HCF of 8 and 32 is 8:

\[8\div8 = 1\]

\[32\div8 = 4\]

\[\boxed{1 : 4}\]

- \(2 : 8\) and \(4 : 16\) are the same ratio, but both numbers can still be divided again.
- \(4 : 1\) swaps the order: the one-euro coins come first.

questions.title: Ch 8 Algebra · Bag of marbles
questions.prompt:
A bag holds \(x\) marbles.

You tip the bag and 9 more marbles into a jar, and the jar has 25 marbles, so \(x + 9 = 25\).

Solve to find \(x\).
questions.figure_alt: A bag of x marbles plus nine marbles equals a jar of 25 marbles; x is a question mark.
questions.solution:
Take 9 from both sides:

\[x + 9 = 25\]

\[x = 25 - 9\]

\[x = \boxed{16}\]

34 adds 9 instead of taking it away.

questions.title: Ch 8 Algebra · Stack of cups
questions.prompt:
A stack of \(c\) paper cups is \(2c + 9\) cm tall, where \(2c + 9\) means \(2\times c + 9\).

How tall is a stack of 7 cups?
questions.figure_alt: A function machine: 7 cups go in, times 2, plus 9, and the height in centimetres is a question mark.
questions.solution:
Put 7 in place of \(c\), multiply first, then add:

\[2\times7 = 14\]

\[14 + 9 = \boxed{23}\]

36 cm reads \(2c\) as 27, but \(2c\) means \(2\times c\).

questions.title: Ch 9 Sequences · Plus-sign tiles
questions.prompt:
Square tiles make a plus sign that grows.

Pattern 1 uses 1 tile, pattern 2 uses 5 and pattern 3 uses 9.

How many tiles does pattern 4 use?
questions.figure_alt: Plus signs of square tiles: 1, 5 and 9 tiles; pattern 4 is a question mark.
questions.solution:
Each new pattern adds 4 tiles:

\[9 + 4 = \boxed{13}\]

10 adds 1 tile, but each pattern adds one tile on each of the 4 arms, so 4 tiles.

questions.title: Ch 9 Sequences · Savings
questions.prompt:
You save money each week.

After week number \(n\) your money box holds \(10n + 4\) euros, where \(10n + 4\) means \(10\times n + 4\).

How many euros are in it after week 7?
questions.figure_alt: A table: weeks 1, 2, 3 give 14, 24, 34 euros (each +10); week 7 is a question mark. The rule is 10n + 4.
questions.solution:
Put \(n = 7\) into the rule, multiply first, then add:

\[10\times7 = 70\]

\[70 + 4 = \boxed{74}\]

€21 reads \(10n\) as 10 + 7, but \(10n\) means \(10\times n\).

questions.title: Ch 10 Circles · Round table
questions.prompt:
A round dining table has radius 60 cm.

Find its diameter.
questions.figure_alt: A round wooden table with a 60 cm radius from the centre and a dashed diameter across it.
questions.solution:
The diameter goes right across, so it is two radii:

\[d = 2r\]

\[d = 2\times60\]

\[d = \boxed{120 \text{ cm}}\]

30 cm halves the radius; the diameter is double, not half.

questions.title: Ch 10 Circles · Roundabout
questions.prompt:
A roundabout has diameter 40 m.

Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) to find the distance once round it (the circumference).
questions.figure_alt: A roundabout of diameter 40 m rolled out into a straight line a little more than 3 diameters long.
questions.solution:
The circumference is about 3.14 diameters:

\[C = \pi d\]

\[C \approx 3.14\times40\]

\[C \approx \boxed{125.6 \text{ m}}\]

62.8 m uses the radius (20 m) instead of the diameter, so it is only half way round.

questions.title: Ch 11 Perimeter & Area · Pool floor
questions.prompt:
The floor of a small swimming pool is 10 m long and 4 m wide.

Find its area.
questions.figure_alt: A 10 m by 4 m pool floor split into 1 m squares.
questions.solution:
Rows of squares:

\[A = l\times w\]

\[A = 10\times4\]

\[A = \boxed{40 \text{ m}^2}\]

28 m is the perimeter (the distance round), not the area.

questions.title: Ch 11 Perimeter & Area · House gable
questions.prompt:
The end wall of a house roof (the gable) is a triangle with base 8 m and height 7 m.

Find its area.
questions.figure_alt: A triangle with base 8 m and height 7 m inside a dashed 8 by 7 rectangle on a grid.
questions.solution:
A triangle is half of its rectangle:

\[A = \tfrac{1}{2}bh\]

\[A = \tfrac{1}{2}\times8\times7\]

\[A = \boxed{28 \text{ m}^2}\]

56 m² forgets the half.

questions.title: Ch 12 Surface Area & Nets · Storage cube
questions.prompt:
A cube-shaped storage box has edges of 10 cm.

Find its surface area.
questions.figure_alt: A cube with 10 cm edges and a net of six squares in a 1–4–1 shape.
questions.solution:
6 square faces, each:

\[\begin{aligned} 10\times10 &= 100 \text{ cm}^2 \\ SA &= 6a^2 \end{aligned}\]

\[SA = 6\times100\]

\[SA = \boxed{600 \text{ cm}^2}\]

1000 cm³ is the volume 10 × 10 × 10; surface area covers the outside.

questions.title: Ch 12 Surface Area & Nets · Ferry container
questions.prompt:
A container on the Gozo ferry is 6 m long, 2 m wide and 3 m high.

Find its volume.
questions.figure_alt: A cuboid 6 by 2 by 3 built from 1 m cubes.
questions.solution:
Count the cubes, layer by layer:

\[V = lwh\]

\[V = 6\times2\times3\]

\[V = \boxed{36 \text{ m}^3}\]

11 m³ adds the three lengths; volume multiplies them.

questions.title: Ch 13 Graphs · Bus stop
questions.prompt:
A street map of a town is drawn on a grid.

The bus stop is at point B.

What are the coordinates of B?
questions.figure_alt: A coordinate grid from 0 to 6 across and 0 to 5 up with point B plotted next to a small picture.
questions.solution:
From 0 go 6 across, then 4 up:

\[\boxed{(6, 4)}\]

\((4, 6)\) reads up before across.

questions.title: Ch 13 Graphs · Bowling
questions.prompt:
At a bowling alley, shoe hire is €4 and each game is €2.

The cost is \(y = 2x + 4\) euros for \(x\) games.

Find \(y\) when \(x = 3\).
questions.figure_alt: The line y = 2x + 4 on a grid; a dashed line from x = 3 goes up to the line at a question mark.
questions.solution:
Put \(x = 3\) into the rule:

\[y = 2\times3 + 4\]

\[y = 6 + 4\]

\[y = \boxed{10}\]

- The answer is €10.
- \(18\) adds \(2 + 4\) first and then multiplies by 3: multiply first.

questions.title: Ch 14 Statistics · Pets at home
questions.prompt:
Eight classmates say how many pets they have at home: \(0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 0, 3, 1\).

Find the mode.
questions.figure_alt: A dot plot of 0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 0, 3, 1: the column above 1 is the tallest.
questions.solution:
The mode is the value that appears most often: 1 appears 4 times.

\[\text{mode} = \boxed{1}\]

\(4\) is how many times 1 appears, not the value itself.

questions.title: Ch 14 Statistics · Seedlings
questions.prompt:
Four seedlings are 5 cm, 9 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm tall.

Find their mean height.
questions.figure_alt: A bar chart of 5, 9, 8, 10; the mean, the level height, is a question mark.
questions.solution:
Add them, then share equally between the 4 values:

\[5 + 9 + 8 + 10 = 32\]

\[32\div4 = \boxed{8}\]

\(32\) is the total; the mean shares it out.

questions.title: Ch 15 Probability · Pencil case
questions.prompt:
A pencil case holds 5 black and 6 blue pens.

You take one pen without looking.

What is the probability that it is black?
questions.figure_alt: Pencil case: 5 black and 6 blue; the probability is a question mark.
questions.solution:
5 black out of:

\[\begin{aligned} 5 + 6 &= 11 \\ P(\text{black}) &= \boxed{\frac{5}{11}} \end{aligned}\]

\(\frac{5}{6}\) compares black with blue; a probability compares with **all** 11 pens.

questions.title: Ch 15 Probability · Box of doughnuts
questions.prompt:
A box has 12 doughnuts: 5 are chocolate and the rest are strawberry.

You take one without looking.

What is the probability that it is **not** chocolate?
questions.figure_alt: A box of 12 doughnuts, 5 chocolate and 7 strawberry.
questions.solution:
\[P(\text{not chocolate}) = 1 - \frac{5}{12}\]

\[P(\text{not chocolate}) = \boxed{\frac{7}{12}}\]

- \(\frac{5}{12}\) is P(chocolate) itself.
- \(\frac{12}{7}\) is more than 1, and no probability is more than 1.

questions.title: Ch 16 Constructions · Climbing frame
questions.prompt:
A playground climbing frame has a triangle made of three metal bars.

Which three lengths can make a triangle?
questions.figure_alt: A base of 7 m with compass arcs of 2 m and 4 m from its ends; the arcs leave a gap and never meet.
questions.solution_title: The two short sides must reach
questions.solution:
The two shorter sides together must be longer than the longest:

\[5 + 5 = 10\]

\[10 > 8\]

- So \(\boxed{5 \text{ m}, 5 \text{ m}, 8 \text{ m}}\) works.
- In the others the short sides are too short: \(2 + 4 = 6\), \(3 + 6 = 9\) and \(1 + 7 = 8\), each less than the longest side.

questions.title: Ch 16 Constructions · Two roads
questions.prompt:
Two roads meet at an angle of \(100^\circ\).

A new footpath bisects the angle between them.

What angle does the footpath make with each road?
questions.figure_alt: An angle of 100° with a dashed bisector splitting it into two equal angles marked with question marks.
questions.solution:
Bisect means cut into two equal halves:

\[100^\circ\div2 = \boxed{50^\circ}\]

\(200^\circ\) doubles instead of halving.

questions.title: Ch 17 Transformations · Window pattern
questions.prompt:
A window pattern is symmetric about the \(x\)-axis.

A star is at \((-2, 3)\).

Where is the matching star?
questions.figure_alt: A grid with the x-axis as a mirror; the point (-2, 3) and a dashed arrow to a question mark on the other side.
questions.solution:
The \(x\)-axis is the mirror: \(y\) changes sign, \(x\) stays.

\[(-2, 3) \to \boxed{(-2, -3)}\]

\((2, 3)\) reflects in the \(y\)-axis instead.

questions.title: Ch 17 Transformations · Town bus
questions.prompt:
On a town map a bus is at \((4, 3)\).

It drives by \(\binom{-3}{-2}\): 3 left and 2 down.

Where does it arrive?
questions.figure_alt: A grid with the point (4, 3), a move of 3 left and 2 down ending at a question mark.
questions.solution:
Add the moves to the coordinates:

\[(4 - 3,\ 3 - 2) = \boxed{(1, 1)}\]

\((-3, -2)\) is the move itself, not where the point lands.

questions.title: Ch 18 Real-life Problems · Bakery
questions.prompt:
At a bakery the bill is €7.85.

You pay with a €20 note.

How much change do you get?
questions.figure_alt: A receipt with a total of €7.85 next to a €20 note; the change is a question mark.
questions.solution:
Change = money paid − cost:

\[20.00 - 7.85 = \boxed{12.15}\]

- The change is €12.15.
- \(13.85\) takes away only the 7 euros and copies the cents instead of taking them away too.

questions.title: Ch 18 Real-life Problems · Swimming lesson
questions.prompt:
A swimming lesson starts at 15:25 and ends at 16:05.

How many minutes is the lesson?
questions.figure_alt: Two clocks: 15:25 and 16:05, with an arrow between them marked question mark minutes.
questions.solution:
Count up to the hour, then on:

\[15{:}25 \to 16{:}00 = 35 \text{ min}\]

\[16{:}00 \to 16{:}05 = 5 \text{ min}\]

\[35 + 5 = \boxed{40 \text{ min}}\]

\(80\) subtracts 1605 − 1525 as ordinary numbers, but an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

questions.title: Ch 19 Logo · Square lawn
questions.prompt:
A robot mower cuts the edge of a square lawn.

Every inside angle is 90°.

The robot mower moves forward 20 steps and turns right, 4 times.

In Logo this is `REPEAT 4 [FD 20 RT ?]`.

- `FD 20` means move forward 20 steps (a length).
- `RT ?` means turn right by ? degrees (an angle).

How many degrees is each turn?
questions.figure_alt: A square walked by a robot mower that starts facing right: arrows 1 to 4 are forward 20 steps each; one inside angle of 90° is marked; at each corner a dashed straight-on line and a right turn marked with a question mark.
questions.solution:
The robot mower turns by how much its direction changes:

- Straight on is a turn of \(0^\circ\).
- Turning round to go back is \(180^\circ\).
- The square's inside angle is \(90^\circ\), so the turn is

\[180^\circ - 90^\circ = \boxed{90^\circ}\]

Check: 4 turns make one full spin, \(4\times90^\circ = 360^\circ\), so the robot mower ends facing right again.

\(4\) is the number of sides and \(20\) is the number of steps; neither is the angle.

questions.title: Ch 19 Logo · Square tile
questions.prompt:
A turtle walks around the edge of a square tile (every inside angle is 90°).

The turtle moves forward 15 steps and turns right at each corner, all the way round.

- `FD 15` means move forward 15 steps (a length).
- `RT` means turn right by that many degrees (an angle).

Which commands draw it?
questions.figure_alt: A square walked by a turtle that starts facing left: arrows 1 to 4 are forward 15 steps each; one inside angle of 90° is marked; at each corner a dashed straight-on line and a right turn marked with a question mark.
questions.solution:
Count the sides and look at one corner:

- The shape has 4 sides, so the commands repeat \(4\) times.
- Straight on (the dashed line) is a turn of \(0^\circ\).
- Turning round to go back is \(180^\circ\).
- The inside angle is \(90^\circ\), so the turn is

\[180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ\]

Check: \(4\times90^\circ = 360^\circ\), one full spin, so the turtle is back at the start, facing left.

\[\boxed{\texttt{REPEAT 4 [FD 15 RT 90]}}\]

`REPEAT 4 [FD 15 RT 360]` uses the full spin for every corner, so the turtle never changes direction and walks in a straight line. `REPEAT 3 [FD 15 RT 90]` repeats only 3 times: \(3\times90^\circ = 270^\circ\), less than a full spin, so the shape does not close. `REPEAT 4 [FD 15 RT 120]` uses the turn for a triangle: \(4\times120^\circ = 480^\circ\), not one full spin of \(360^\circ\).

takeaway:
- Draw it first: a picture shows which rule to use.
- Check that the answer makes sense in the picture.
